definitions.gloss: intestinal medicine; probiotic supplement; digestive regulator
definitions.explanation: Medicine that regulates intestinal function and restores the balance of gut bacteria. Commonly taken for diarrhea, constipation, bloating, and general digestive discomfort.

examples.japanese: おなかの{調子|ちょうし}が{悪|わる}いので{整腸剤|せいちょうざい}を{飲|の}んだ。
examples.english: My stomach was off, so I took some intestinal medicine.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}に{整腸剤|せいちょうざい}を{処方|しょほう}された。
examples.english: The doctor prescribed me digestive medicine.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}{中|ちゅう}はおなかを{壊|こわ}しやすいので、{整腸剤|せいちょうざい}を{持|も}っていくといい。
examples.english: It's easy to get an upset stomach while traveling, so it's good to bring intestinal medicine with you.

notes:
A common over-the-counter medication in Japan. Popular brands include ビオフェルミン and ミヤリサン. These typically contain beneficial bacteria (probiotics) to restore intestinal balance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {整腸剤|せいちょうざい}を{飲|の}む: to take digestive medicine
- {整腸剤|せいちょうざい}を{処方|しょほう}する: to prescribe digestive medicine
- {市販|しはん}の{整腸剤|せいちょうざい}: over-the-counter digestive medicine

RELATED WORDS:
- {胃腸薬|いちょうやく}: stomach and intestinal medicine — broader category
- {下痢止|げりど}め: anti-diarrheal medicine
- {便秘薬|べんぴやく}: laxative

FORMS:
{整腸|せいちょう} (regulating the intestines) + {剤|ざい} (medicine/agent)
